ch32.note: The three-man body set up in January 1946 to halt the civil war: the U.S. special envoy George Marshall, the Nationalist representative Zhang Qun, and the Communist representative Zhou Enlai. It directed the Beiping truce apparatus, and its brief, failed mediation is the backdrop to all of Part Four.
Zhang Qun (张群, 1889–1990), a senior Nationalist statesman and lifelong intimate of Chiang Kai-shek, who served as the government's representative in the postwar mediation.

Zhou Enlai (周恩来, 1898–1976), a foremost leader of the Chinese Communist Party, its representative in these negotiations and, from 1949 until his death, the first Premier of the People's Republic of China.

The tripartite body—American, Nationalist, and Communist—established at Beiping in 1946 to supervise the cease-fire on the ground (in English usually the 'Executive Headquarters'). Its field teams and its collapse frame the fighting Chen describes.

Ye Jianying (叶剑英, 1897–1986), the Communist chief of staff at the Beiping Executive Headquarters, later one of the ten marshals of the People's Liberation Army and, in his last years, titular head of state of the People's Republic.

Li Zongren (李宗仁, 1891–1969), the Guangxi-clique leader who headed the Nationalists' Beiping Field Headquarters in this period; in 1949, as the regime collapsed, he became Acting President of the Republic of China.
Magong (Makung), the chief town of the Penghu (Pescadores) Islands in the Taiwan Strait, a Nationalist-held stepping-stone on the retreat from the mainland to Taiwan.
